page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 3 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates one physical core with two threads. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It features dedicated CPU allocation and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and excels in single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3. However, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores fall into the lower quartile due to the low core count. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom decile, and small-block memory bandwidth is weak, though large-block read and write bandwidths maintain average tiering.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-highcpu-2 provides an economical entry point for workloads requiring dedicated, high-performance single-core execution without the overhead of massive memory allocations. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.5 GB per core limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications. This instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded processing, basic static web serving, simple utility scripts, and low-concurrency tasks that benefit from modern AMD EPYC instruction sets but do not require extensive RAM or local storage.

This instance provides a single physical core with two threads and dedicated CPU allocation, but lacks local storage and GPU resources. Performance benchmarks highlight exceptional single-core capabilities, with top-tier results in single-threaded stress-ng, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression. Conversely, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are limited, with Passmark memory scores falling into the lowest decile. This resource profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for workloads that demand strong single-threaded CPU performance but have minimal memory requirements. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded utility scripts, and basic background processing tasks.
